title: Firewall Basics: Defending a School Network
summary: An attacker is probing your school's network. Investigate the alerts, block dangerous services and a malicious address, keep the school website online, and apply the firewall policy.
subject: cybersecurity
objectives: Read security alerts and identify the attacked services
Write firewall rules that block telnet (23) and remote desktop (3389)
Block a known malicious IP address
Explain the principle of least privilege

steps.title: Start your shift
steps.instruction: Log in to the analyst workstation.
steps.say: Welcome to the ECH Cyber Operations Center. Our school network is under attack, so let's find out what's happening.
hints: Select the workstation and choose the 'login' command.

steps.title: Investigate
steps.instruction: Run 'show alerts' to see what the attacker is trying.
steps.say: The alerts show repeated login attempts on port 23 (telnet) and port 3389 (remote desktop), all from 203.0.113.66.

question.prompt: Why is telnet (port 23) dangerous on the internet?
choices: It sends usernames and passwords unencrypted
question.explanation: Telnet sends everything, including passwords, in plain text that anyone on the path can read. SSH replaced it.

steps.title: Block telnet
steps.instruction: On the edge firewall, add a rule that denies telnet (port 23).
hints: Select the firewall and choose 'deny 23 telnet'.

steps.title: Block remote desktop
steps.instruction: Deny remote desktop (port 3389) from the internet.

steps.title: Keep the website online
steps.instruction: Students still need the school website. Allow HTTPS (port 443).

steps.title: Report
steps.instruction: How many threat-blocking rules did you add?

question.prompt: The firewall's policy is 'default-deny'. What does that mean?
choices: Everything is blocked unless a rule allows it
Everything is allowed unless a rule blocks it
Only teachers can use the internet
The firewall turns off at night
question.explanation: Default-deny follows the principle of least privilege: only traffic you explicitly need is allowed.

hazards.message: Danger! You just ALLOWED a service the attacker is targeting. Remove that rule's effect by denying it again.
